Tabelog could not be checked: as of 2026-09-02 it still returns HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare bot-challenge body to both curl and WebFetch, so its page for this shop is UNVERIFIED rather than empty and its URL is deliberately absent from sources. Nothing here needed it. ⚠ THE NAME IS THE THING TO UNDERSTAND, AND IT IS NOT A GLUTEN CLAIM. 玄蕎麦 means WHOLE, UNHULLED buckwheat — the grain milled with its husk, which is a flavour and colour claim, not a purity one. It says nothing about how much wheat flour is blended in as つなぎ, and the shop does not publish a ratio anywhere on this page. Japanese soba is normally 二八, eight parts buckwheat to two parts WHEAT, and a coeliac who reads 玄蕎麦 as "pure buckwheat" has made the single most expensive misreading available in a Japanese noodle shop. Even a confirmed 十割 kitchen dusts its boards with 打ち粉 — usually wheat flour — and boils every order of the day in the same pot of water. So every soba bowl below is flagged against, and the honest position is that this is a place a coeliac eats around rather than at. ⚠ THE SIDE DISHES ARE WHERE THE ACTUAL FOOD IS, and one of them is a genuine find: 湯葉刺し, raw yuba, is soybean skin and nothing else — fully vegan, and the only thing on this menu a vegan can order as a dish. It arrives with soy sauce, which is the wheat, so ask for it plain or bring tamari. ⚠ AND THE DRINKS LIST HAS A TRAP WORTH NAMING: 浅草蕎麦湯ブラン is built on 蕎麦湯, the cloudy water the soba was boiled in — which is to say the water carrying the day’s 打ち粉. It is the one drink on the board that is a gluten question rather than a soft one. 蕎麦焼酎 十割 is a second, subtler one: buckwheat shochu is very often fermented with 麦麹, BARLEY koji, and 麦 is not on Japan’s statutory allergen list so nobody is required to declare it.

tokyo_dogenzaka_tamagoken.price_note: Full menu with prices, read from the shop’s own official page for this branch, which states 表記は税込価格 — prices shown include tax. The page also carries the practicalities: 11:00–22:00 with last orders at 21:30, 渋谷区道玄坂2-25-12 道玄坂通1階, counter 6 and tables 24, and ordering is by MOBILE QR CODE at the table rather than by speaking to anyone. ⚠ THAT LAST DETAIL MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS FOR A COELIAC: a QR ordering system has no field for "no flour in the sauce", and the person who brings the plate is not the person who could answer. If a question needs asking here, it has to be asked deliberately at the counter, not typed into the tablet. ⚠ THE DISH IS EGG OVER RICE, AND THE SAUCE IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM. An omurice itself is a thin omelette over rice — no wheat in either — which makes this one of the more promising formats in Japan until you read the sauce list. This kitchen sells the dish BY sauce, and the two house sauces are the two worst cases: ハヤシ is a demi-glace, which is by definition built on a browned FLOUR ROUX, and Japanese curry is a roux in solid brick form. The kitchen’s own sauce list — ハヤシ, トマト, キノコクリーム, 明太子, バジルトマト — is reproduced at the end of this record as options rather than dishes, because that is how the page lists them, with no prices. ⚠ AND A VEGAN CANNOT EAT HERE AT ALL. The shop is an オムライス専門店 — an omelette-rice specialist — so egg is not an ingredient in the dishes, it IS the dish. The only items on the whole board without egg are the chips.

items.en: Hayashi omurice — omelette rice in demi-glace
items.note: ⚠ HAYASHI SAUCE IS A FLOUR ROUX. Hayashi is the Japanese demi-glace — beef and onion in a browned sauce whose thickening agent is WHEAT FLOUR cooked in fat. It is the shop’s default and its cheapest dish, which makes it the one a coeliac is most likely to be handed by accident. Beef, and normally butter and red wine as well. Every omurice here is wrapped in EGG, so nothing in this section reaches a vegan.

THE MOST PROMISING DISH ON THE BOARD, and still a question rather than a yes. A tomato sauce needs no roux, so this is the one sauce here that could be free of flour — but the page does not say how it is made, and the rice underneath a Japanese omurice is usually チキンライス fried with ketchup and sometimes a splash of Worcester-style sauce, which would be wheat. Worth asking about both the sauce and the rice. Every omurice here is wrapped in EGG, so nothing in this section reaches a vegan.

tokyo_urashima_tarou.price_note: Full menu with prices, tax included, read from the shop’s own official page and the two Gnavi menu pages it links — okonomiyaki, monja, toppings, griddle dishes, foil-baked plates, salads, rice and noodles, and desserts. The page notes that TAKEAWAY IS TAXED DIFFERENTLY, so these prices are the eat-in ones. 千代田区神田三崎町3-7-12 原田ビル4F, two minutes from Suidobashi, open every day 16:00–23:30 (L.O. 23:00), no closing day. ⚠ THIS IS THE HARDEST FORMAT IN THE DATASET FOR A COELIAC, AND IT IS WORTH SAYING PLAINLY. Okonomiyaki and monjayaki are wheat-flour batter by definition — but the deeper problem is not the dish, it is the GRIDDLE. The shop’s own description is 当店ではお好み焼きももんじゃ焼きも、ご自分で作って楽しんでいただくスタイル: you cook it yourself on the teppan set into your table. Every 鉄板焼き item on this menu — the mushrooms, the scallops, the vegetable platter — is cooked on that SAME plate, minutes after someone spread wheat batter across it by hand. There is no version of this meal where a naturally wheat-free ingredient reaches the plate without touching that surface, which is why the griddle dishes below are flagged against on gluten even where their ingredients are clean. The safe items here are the cold ones. ⚠ AND THE BATTER IS A VEGAN FACT AS WELL AS A GLUTEN ONE. The shop advertises 生地には豊洲から取り寄せた鰹節でしっかり取った出汁を使用 — the batter is mixed with a bonito dashi made from Toyosu katsuobushi. That is offered as a quality boast, and it means the plainest vegetable okonomiyaki on the board contains FISH in its flour. A vegan reading this menu for a vegetable option will not find one, and nothing in any dish name says so. ⚠ TWO NAMES THAT HIDE WHEAT: ベビースター, at ¥748 and again as a ¥176 topping, is Baby Star — the snack made of FRIED INSTANT RAMEN, so it is wheat noodles crushed over a wheat pancake. And 広島風そばのせ means a layer of yakisoba NOODLES laid inside the okonomiyaki, Hiroshima style, which is wheat noodles on top of wheat batter. ⚠ THE ONE GENUINE PROSPECT is ざる豆腐 at ¥528 — chilled tofu, off the griddle, plant from start to finish, limited only by what is poured on it.
